entries.title: Set a separate headshot and bio for each event a speaker appears in
entries.summary: Organizers and speakers can now store a distinct **Event Headshot** and **Event Bio** for each event, independent of the contact's org-level profile. The event-specific values appear on embeds, Sites speaker pages, agenda cards, integration syncs, exports, headshot zips, and the Public API — everywhere the contact's own values previously appeared. Writing an event override never changes the contact record, and writing the contact record never changes an event override.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable event-specific headshot and bio; then Contacts → [contact] → Profile (admin) or the speaker portal profile page

entries.use_case: Organisations that run multiple events with the same speakers — such as a flagship conference and a regional roadshow — can give each speaker a tailored bio and headshot per event without overwriting the speaker's master profile. Speakers can update their own event-specific details from their portal without affecting other events they are part of.

cs_action.note: This is a limited release targeting Tahaluf initially. Reach out to confirm the customer's use case before enabling; the feature adds a new DB table and new API fields (photo_url_source, headshotSource, bioSource) that downstream integrations may need to handle.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains that updating a speaker's bio or headshot for one event breaks another event, or when they manage speakers who appear across multiple events with different branding needs.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who run multiple events per year with overlapping speaker rosters and need per-event speaker profiles — particularly large associations and multi-event organisations like Tahaluf.
internal.staff_path: Contacts → [contact] → Profile (admin GET/PUT /contacts/event/:eventId/:recordId/event-profile); Speaker portal → Profile page (event_profile fields)
internal.gotchas: The table starts empty — no backfill — so all existing payloads are unchanged until an organizer or speaker sets an override. A cross-org event clone does not copy overrides (contacts are recreated). The bio override replaces the bio in every language for that event. If a Headshot or Bio field is hidden or locked for a role, the admin endpoint returns 403. CFP form field mapping to the override, webhooks, and email merge tags are not yet built.
internal.talk_track: If the same speaker presents at your annual summit and your regional workshop, you can now give them a different headshot and bio for each — without touching their master profile. They can even update it themselves from their speaker portal, and it flows straight to your website embeds and event app.

draft.docs_gap: The contact-profile guide should add a section explaining event-specific headshot and bio overrides: how to set them as an admin (via the contact profile for a given event), how speakers set them from their portal, how the resolver picks the event value over the org value, which surfaces display the override, and what happens during event clone and contact merge.
draft.why_use_it: A contact in Sessionboard is an org-level record, so a speaker's headshot and bio are shared across every event they appear in. Event-specific overrides let you store a distinct photo and biography for each event independently. The event's values flow automatically to embeds, Sites, agenda cards, integration syncs, headshot downloads, and the Public API, so every surface shows the right version without manual workarounds. Speakers can set their own event overrides from their portal, and organizers can manage them from the contact profile — neither action touches the other event's data.

entries.title: Collect payments on sponsor and exhibitor intake forms
entries.summary: Intake forms for sponsors and exhibitors can now charge a fee at submission. In the form's new **Pricing & payment** step, set a base fee, connect a Spreedly payment gateway, add conditional pricing rules (for example, Tier = Gold → $5,000), VAT rules, and promo codes. Submitters who owe a fee land on a payment step after completing the form; their group shows **Pending Payment** until the card clears. Paid submissions trigger a confirmation email and an **Invoice Receipt** notification. Invoices appear under **Invoices → Sponsor & exhibitor intake forms**, support refunds, and add **Payment status**, **Invoice number**, **Amount**, and **Paid at** columns to Sponsors and Exhibitors exports. New `sponsor.payment.status.changed` and `exhibitor.payment.status.changed` webhooks fire on each status transition.

enable.path: Sponsors (or Exhibitors) → Intake form → Pricing & payment → Upon Submission

where.path: Sponsors → Intake form → Pricing & payment; Exhibitors → Intake form → Pricing & payment; Sessions → Invoices → Sponsor & exhibitor intake forms

entries.use_case: Event teams that charge sponsors or exhibitors a participation fee can now collect payment directly through the intake form, eliminating the need to invoice separately. Conditional pricing rules let you charge different amounts by tier automatically, and promo codes support discounts or fully waived fees.

cs_action.note: Only 4 US orgs currently have both an intake form and a Spreedly gateway. Proactively reach out to customers who use intake forms and charge sponsors/exhibitors outside Sessionboard today.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to collect sponsor or exhibitor fees, or when they mention invoicing sponsors manually after intake form submissions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using sponsor or exhibitor intake forms who currently collect fees outside Sessionboard (separate invoice, payment link, etc.).
internal.staff_path: Sponsors → Intake form → Pricing & payment (admin config); Sessions → Invoices → Sponsor & exhibitor intake forms (invoice list and refunds)
internal.gotchas: Every existing intake form defaults to pricing_type = 'none', so no existing form is affected at deploy. A Spreedly payment gateway must already be connected at the org level (Settings → Payments) before the pricing step can be saved. Refunds are staff-only (superUserOnly). The confirmation email is held until payment clears for paid forms; free forms send it on submission as before.
internal.talk_track: If you charge sponsors or exhibitors a fee to participate, you can now collect that payment right inside the intake form. Set your base fee, add tier-based rules so Gold sponsors pay more than Silver automatically, and optionally give certain contacts a promo code for a discount. Sessionboard handles the payment step, sends a receipt, and tracks every invoice so your finance team always knows who has paid.

draft.docs_gap: Both the sponsor and exhibitor intake form guides should add a section covering the Pricing & payment step: setting a base fee, connecting a gateway, adding pricing rules and VAT rules, creating promo codes, the submitter payment flow, the Pending Payment group status, the Invoice Receipt notification, the Invoices page filter for intake forms, refunds, export columns, and the payment status webhooks.
draft.why_use_it: Intake forms let sponsors and exhibitors submit their information and complete payment in a single, unassisted flow. Set a base fee, add tier-based pricing rules, and connect your Spreedly gateway — Sessionboard handles the payment step, tracks invoice status, and sends receipts automatically. All paid and pending invoices are visible in one place alongside your other event invoices, with export columns and webhooks to keep your finance records in sync.

entries.title: Session field filters in email campaigns now return correct audience counts
entries.summary: Filters on session fields — including **Tags**, **Track**, **Format**, **Level**, **Language**, **Location**, **Status**, and custom session fields — now resolve correctly when building a campaign audience. Previously, combining a submission-status filter with a session tag or custom field filter (for example, "Submission status is Pending" + "Tags is Poster Queue") returned 0 recipients even when matching sessions existed; the correct audience is now shown in previews, scheduled sends, automated emails, and recipient counts.

where.path: Communications → Email Campaigns → New Campaign → Audience filters

entries.use_case: An organizer building a targeted campaign — for example, emailing only the participants of pending "Poster Queue" sessions — can now combine submission-status and session-tag filters and trust that the audience count reflects the real number of matching people.

cs_action.note: 9 stored campaigns in US and 4 in EU carry UUID session field rows; all were draft or cancelled so no scheduled send changed, but customers who noticed 0-recipient counts on session-field filters should be told the bug is fixed and invited to rebuild those campaigns.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that adding a Tags, Track, Format, Level, Language, Location, Status, or custom session field filter to a campaign audience drops the count to 0.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who uses session-field audience filters in email campaigns, especially those who noticed unexpectedly empty audiences since April 2026.
internal.staff_path: Communications → Email Campaigns → campaign → Audience
internal.gotchas: The fix also corrects automated emails, Advocacy dynamic audiences, Reach audiences, and the GenAI recipient count — all share the same filter resolver. Campaigns that were saved with broken filters will now show the correct (higher) count when reopened.
internal.talk_track: If you ever filtered a campaign audience by a session tag or custom session field and got 0 recipients, that was a bug — it's now fixed. Rebuild those audience filters and you'll see the correct count.

draft.docs_gap: The email-campaigns guide should note which session fields are supported as audience filters (Tags, Track, Format, Level, Language, Location, Status, and custom session fields) and explain how combining them with submission-status filters works.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Add a payment card before sending emails in self-serve workspaces
entries.summary: Self-serve workspaces now prompt you to add a payment card the first time you try to send a message that requires one, instead of showing an error. Clicking any send button that needs a card opens an **Add a card to send** dialog, which launches Stripe's secure card setup page. After you return, the card is confirmed and the send proceeds. This applies to Sessions decision emails, Awards announcements and reviewer invites, Learning bulk emails, CRM agreement sends, and Marketing campaign launches. Previews, drafts, and test sends are unaffected.

where.path: Any send action (Sessions → Decision Emails; Awards → Announce / Reviewer Invites; Learning → Bulk Email; CRM → Agreements; Marketing → Campaigns)

entries.use_case: When a self-serve customer tries to send their first decision email, reviewer invite, or campaign and has no card on file, they are guided through adding one in-context rather than hitting a dead end. This removes a common friction point that would otherwise block a send mid-workflow.

cs_action.note: Applies only to self-serve workspaces. Platform orgs never see this dialog — the API never returns card_required to a Platform org.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding a self-serve customer who is about to send their first decision emails, reviewer invites, or campaign.
internal.who_should_get_it: Self-serve customers on CRM, Awards, Learning, Sessions, or Marketing workspaces who have not yet added a payment card.
internal.gotchas: Previews, drafts, and test sends bypass the card check entirely. The dialog only fires on a real send. Marketing campaign launch keeps the draft open and reopens the dialog if the API refuses — the draft is not lost.
internal.talk_track: The first time you hit Send in your workspace, if there is no card on file, a dialog walks you through adding one via Stripe. It charges nothing at that step — it just saves the card so future sends go straight through.

draft.docs_gap: The CRM plan-and-billing guide (and its counterparts for Marketing, Learning, Awards, and Sessions) should add a section explaining the card-on-file requirement for sends, how the Add a card to send dialog works, and which send actions trigger it versus which are exempt (previews, drafts, test sends).
draft.why_use_it: Self-serve workspaces require a payment card on file before emails and campaigns can be sent to people. The **Add a card to send** flow lets you add your card at the exact moment you need it — directly from the send button — without navigating away to billing settings. Once the card is saved, your send goes out immediately.

entries.title: Drive all of Sessionboard Learning from an AI assistant via the Public API
entries.summary: The Public API now exposes the full Sessionboard Learning surface under **`/v1/learning/...`** and **`/v1/organization/:orgId/learning/...`**, making every major Learning workflow reachable from Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or any MCP-connected assistant. Covered endpoints include certifications (create, read, update), assignments (list, nudge, delete), quiz reviews and grading, submission decisions, learner activity, communications and nudges, credit goals, reports and exports, learning sites, translations, and course feedback settings. Writes that affect learners or the public — such as publishing a certification, sending reminders, or pushing translations live — return a **202 needs_approval** response so a human can confirm before the change takes effect.

where.path: Learning → (any section) — via AI assistant or API client using an org-wide key with read:learning / write:learning scopes

entries.use_case: Learning administrators who use Claude, ChatGPT or a custom MCP connector can now manage the entire Learning lifecycle — from creating certifications and assigning training to grading quizzes, nudging learners, running reports and updating the learning site — without leaving their AI assistant. Writes that reach learners still pause for human approval, keeping the organizer in control.

cs_action.note: Additive API routes only; no UI change. Existing Learning customers get expanded AI-assistant coverage automatically when using an org-wide API key.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Learning customer asks how to automate certification workflows, bulk-assign training, or manage their learning programme from an AI assistant.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already on Sessionboard Learning who use or want to use the MCP connector or Public API with Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or a custom integration.
internal.staff_path: Learning → (any section) — accessed via API or MCP connector
internal.gotchas: Only org-wide API keys with read:learning / write:learning scopes work; event-scoped keys are refused. Writes that reach learners or the public (publish certification, send reminders, push translations, grade submissions) return 202 needs_approval — the change does not apply until a human confirms in the Sessionboard UI.
internal.talk_track: Your AI assistant can now run your entire Learning programme — assign courses, chase learners who haven't finished, grade written answers and pull credit reports — all by chat. Any change that learners would see still pauses for your OK before it goes live.

draft.docs_gap: The /sessionboard-learning/ask guide should list the newly available API actions (certifications, assignments, quiz grading, submission decisions, learner comms, credit goals, reports, learning sites, translations) and note that learner-facing writes return a 202 needs_approval response requiring human confirmation.
draft.why_use_it: Ask lets you manage Sessionboard Learning by typing plain questions and instructions to your AI assistant. You can build courses, assign training, grade written answers, send nudges, pull credit reports and update your learning site — all without navigating the admin UI. Because writes that affect learners wait for your explicit approval, you stay in control of what learners actually see.

entries.title: AI agents can now read quiz answer files and task submission files before proposing a grade
entries.summary: Two new API endpoints let AI agents retrieve uploaded files from Learning before scoring them. `GET /v1/learning/quiz-reviews/{attemptId}/files/{questionId}` returns the file a learner uploaded for a specific quiz question; `GET /v1/learning/submissions/{progressId}/file` returns the file attached to a task submission. Both return a short-lived `{ url, filename }` link and require an org-wide API key with the `read:learning` scope.
entries.use_case: Teams using AI agents to auto-grade Learning quizzes or task submissions that include file uploads can now have the agent fetch and read the file before proposing a score, removing the need for a human to relay the file contents manually.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is building an AI grading workflow on top of the Learning API and their quizzes or tasks include file-upload questions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Learning module with file-upload quiz questions or task submissions who are building or evaluating AI-assisted grading via the public API.
internal.gotchas: Endpoints accept org-wide API keys only (not event-scoped keys); the returned URL is short-lived, so agents must fetch and process the file promptly after calling the endpoint.
internal.talk_track: If you're using an AI agent to grade learner submissions that include uploaded files, these two new endpoints let the agent pull the file directly so it can read the content before proposing a score — no manual relay needed.

draft.docs_gap: The score-written-answers guide should add a section explaining how to use the two new API endpoints to retrieve quiz-question files and task-submission files for AI-assisted grading, including the required scope and the short-lived URL behaviour.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Learning lets you add written-answer and file-upload questions to quizzes and task submissions, then score them by hand or with an AI agent. These endpoints give an agent the file it needs to read a learner's work — a document, image, or other attachment — so it can propose a grade with full context. Use them when you want to automate or assist grading at scale without losing the nuance of file-based answers.

entries.title: AI assistants can now manage registration forms, archive events, send tours, control ads, handle report shares, retry transcripts, and enable the website tag in Marketing
entries.summary: Ten previously UI-only Marketing actions are now available through the Public API, so AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini) connected via MCP or OAuth can complete end-to-end Marketing workflows without human hand-offs. Assistants can read, reorder and add questions on an event page's **Registration Form**; archive or restore a mistaken event; send **Tour** invitations; rewrite in-person event email copy; list and revoke read-only **Report** share links; pause and resume a running **Ad**; pick the LinkedIn ad account; re-run a failed transcript; manage **Sign-up Form** questions; and turn on the **Website Tag**.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Marketing

where.path: Marketing (via connected AI assistant or Public API)

entries.use_case: A marketing team using Claude or ChatGPT to run their event promotion can now ask their assistant to archive a cancelled event, pause an underperforming ad, add a question to the registration form, or turn on the website tag — all without switching to the Sessionboard UI. This closes the last gaps that required a human to finish the job.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is already using an AI assistant with Sessionboard Marketing and asks why certain actions still require them to open the UI.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Marketing beta who have connected Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or Gemini via MCP or OAuth.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → (via connected AI assistant or Public API token)
internal.gotchas: Destructive actions (archive event, delete a share link, pause an ad) require approval in web-api before the assistant can execute them — the assistant will surface an approval prompt rather than acting silently. No existing API rows were changed; this is purely additive.
internal.talk_track: Your AI assistant can now handle the full Marketing setup loop — registration form questions, ad controls, website tag, tour sends and more — without you needing to jump into the UI for the last few steps.

draft.docs_gap: The /sessionboard-marketing/apps guide should add a section listing which Marketing actions AI assistants can perform via the Public API, including the approval flow for destructive operations such as archiving an event or pausing an ad.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting an AI assistant to Sessionboard Marketing lets your team run campaigns, manage events, control ads, and publish pages through natural-language conversation. The assistant reads your data, drafts changes, and waits for your approval before anything goes live — so you stay in control while moving faster. Use it when you want to delegate repetitive setup tasks or get answers about campaign performance without hunting through menus.

entries.title: Actions run by a connected AI assistant no longer require a second approval in Sessionboard
entries.summary: When Claude, ChatGPT or another connected assistant runs a Marketing action, Sessionboard now treats the assistant's own confirmation prompt as sufficient approval and executes the action immediately — no separate **Approvals** step in Sessionboard is created. The previous behaviour (a **202 needs_approval** response and an entry on the **Approvals** page) is preserved for orgs that turn on the **assistant_approvals** org feature flag.

where.path: Marketing → (any action triggered via a connected AI assistant)

entries.use_case: Teams using Claude or ChatGPT to run Marketing actions no longer have to approve the same action twice — once in the assistant and again inside Sessionboard. The assistant's built-in confirmation is the approval, so work moves faster without an extra click.

cs_action.note: Orgs that want the old double-approval behaviour can have the 'assistant_approvals' org feature flag turned on by staff. With the flag on, assistant-triggered actions still produce a 202 needs_approval response and an Approvals row, exactly as before.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains that running Marketing actions through Claude or ChatGPT requires too many confirmation steps.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using a connected AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) to trigger Marketing actions — the change is on by default for all orgs.
internal.staff_path: Org Admin Settings → Features → assistant_approvals (to restore the old behaviour)
internal.gotchas: If the feature flag lookup fails at runtime, Sessionboard falls back to requiring its own approval, so the old flow is the safe fallback. Human-only writes, the Ask chat grant, the Approvals pages and list_approvals are all unchanged.
internal.talk_track: Your assistant already asks you before it does anything in Sessionboard — that click is your approval. Sessionboard now honours it and runs the action straight away, so you're not clicking twice for the same thing.

draft.docs_gap: The /sessionboard-marketing/apps guide's "Waiting for your OK" section should be updated to explain that assistant-triggered actions now run immediately on the assistant's own confirmation, and that the double-approval behaviour can be restored via the assistant_approvals org feature flag.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing integrates with Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP-compatible assistants so your team can draft campaigns, publish content and trigger actions by chat. Each assistant already asks the person to confirm before any write or destructive tool runs; Sessionboard records every action in the activity log so you always have a full audit trail. Use the assistant connection when you want to move quickly through repetitive marketing tasks without leaving your AI tool of choice.

entries.title: CRM and billing scopes now available to AI assistants connected via OAuth
entries.summary: AI assistants (such as Claude) that connect to Sessionboard via OAuth can now read and write CRM data and retrieve billing links without extra configuration. The `read:crm`, `write:crm`, `read:billing`, and `write:billing` scopes are included in every new client's default scope ceiling, so CRM tools in the connector no longer return a **403 Token missing required scope** error on first connect.
entries.use_case: Any organizer using Claude or another AI assistant to query or update CRM contacts and accounts will now get a working connection on first setup, without needing to manually request additional scopes or contact support.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that their Claude or other AI assistant connector cannot read CRM data or gets a 403 error on CRM tools — this is now fixed for any client registered after 2026-11-14; customers with older clients should reconnect.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the OAuth-based AI assistant integration who also has CRM enabled.
internal.gotchas: Existing connector clients registered before 2026-11-14 will not automatically gain the new scopes — they pick them up the next time the assistant reconnects and registers a new client (Claude does this on every reconnect). write:team, registrations, and expo scopes remain preview-only and are not included.
internal.talk_track: If your Claude connector was returning errors when trying to look up or update CRM contacts, reconnecting it will fix the issue — the CRM and billing scopes are now part of every new client's default access.

draft.docs_gap: The OAuth guide's Available Scopes section should note that read:crm, write:crm, read:billing, and write:billing are now in the default supported scope ceiling, and clarify which scopes remain preview-only (write:team, registrations, expo).
draft.why_use_it: OAuth 2.1 lets you connect Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot and other AI assistants to Sessionboard so they can read and act on your event data on your behalf. Each assistant registers a client and receives a set of scopes that define what it is allowed to do; the default ceiling determines what is available without any extra steps. With CRM and billing scopes in the default ceiling, assistants can look up contacts, update records, and retrieve payment links the moment they connect.

entries.title: AI assistants can now pick winners, edit the nomination form, and check the awards site before opening nominations
entries.summary: Three new capabilities land for AI assistants (Ask, Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) connected to Awards. An assistant can now **Record winners** on your behalf — the action pauses for your approval before saving, and the winner is recorded as you once you approve. An assistant can also read and rewrite the **Nomination Form** questions (adding, reordering, or updating fields while preserving system questions, conditions, and settings), with a revision guard to prevent conflicting edits. Finally, the program detail response now includes the **Awards Site** the form lives on — or the site that would be created when nominations open — so an assistant can warn you before triggering site creation.
entries.use_case: An organizer using an AI assistant to run their awards program can now ask it to record winners and update nomination form questions without leaving the chat — every winner change pauses for human approval before it saves, so nothing is committed without a deliberate sign-off.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Awards also has an AI assistant (Ask, Claude, ChatGPT) connected and wants to automate more of the awards workflow.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Awards add-on who have connected an AI assistant via MCP or use Ask.
internal.staff_path: Awards → Programs → [program] → Winners; Awards → Programs → [program] → Nomination Form
internal.gotchas: Winner recording always requires human approval in the Sessionboard UI — the assistant cannot bypass this. internal.talk_track: Your AI assistant can now handle more of the awards workflow end-to-end: updating the nomination form, checking which site nominations will open on, and recording winners — with every winner pick pausing for your OK before anything is saved.

The MCP server guide should list the new awards tools (form PUT, winners PUT with approval, program GET with site info).
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Awards lets you run the full awards lifecycle — from opening nominations to picking winners — through an AI assistant connected via the MCP server or Ask. The assistant can draft and update your nomination form, assign reviewers, and surface results, always pausing for your approval before recording winners or publishing changes. Use it to move faster on routine program tasks without switching between screens.

entries.title: AI assistants can now manage more Awards program actions, including archiving programs, removing reviewers, managing nominations, setting public vote, selecting winners, and pulling reports
entries.summary: Seven additional Awards workspace actions are now available to AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini) connected via MCP: archive a program, remove a reviewer, remove a nomination, update the **Public Vote** setting, update the **Nomination Form** questions, record **Winners** (with a 202 approval step before the change is saved), and run or export **Reports**. entries.use_case: An organizer using Claude or ChatGPT can now ask their AI assistant to remove a reviewer from a program, close nominations, update the nomination form, enable public voting, or pull an awards report — without switching to the Sessionboard UI. internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with Awards and an MCP-connected AI assistant asks what their assistant can do in Awards, or when they want to reduce manual admin work during the review and winner-selection phase.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who have Awards enabled and have already connected an AI assistant via MCP.
internal.staff_path: Awards → Programs (read via MCP server)
internal.gotchas: Winner selection returns a 202 needs_approval response — the assistant will surface this for human confirmation before the record is written. internal.talk_track: Your AI assistant can now handle the day-to-day Awards admin — removing reviewers, tweaking the nomination form, enabling public voting, and pulling reports — all by chat. When it comes to picking winners, it will always pause and ask you to confirm before anything is saved.

draft.docs_gap: The MCP Server guide should add a section listing all available Awards workspace actions (archive program, remove reviewer, remove nomination, public vote, nomination form, winners with approval, reports) and note that the winners action returns a 202 needs_approval response requiring human confirmation.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting an AI assistant to Sessionboard lets you manage your awards program by conversation. Ask about submission counts, assign reviewers, adjust the nomination form, or pull a report — the assistant reads and writes directly to your program. Actions that change winners pause for your explicit approval before anything is saved, so you stay in control of the most consequential decisions.

entries.title: Create a Sessions event from a conference page URL, get clearer redirect messages, and approve speaker emails from an AI assistant

entries.use_case: Teams using Claude, ChatGPT or another MCP-connected assistant to set up Sessions events can now point the assistant at a conference website URL and get a correctly configured event back in one step. internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is using or evaluating MCP / AI-assistant workflows with Sessionboard Sessions, or when they report that importing an event from a URL created the wrong event type.

draft.docs_gap: The speaker-emails guide should add a section explaining the approval gate for AI assistants (needs_approval behaviour), and the Sessions get-started or MCP guide should document the import-from-URL capability including the dry-run preview option and how redirect errors are surfaced.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's AI agent support lets you set up and manage a Sessions event entirely through a connected assistant like Claude or ChatGPT. You can describe what you need in plain language — create an event, open a call for speakers, schedule sessions, or email accepted speakers — and the assistant carries out each step, pausing for your approval on actions that send communications or publish content. entries.title: Import a Sessions event from its public page and manage the speaker emails plan via the API
entries.summary: Four new API routes extend the Sessions workspace so AI agents and integrations can do everything the self-serve Sessions pages do. `POST /sessions-workspace/events/import-url` imports a Sessions event from its public page URL; pass `dryRun: true` to preview the import before committing. `GET /events/:eventId/coordinator`, `PUT …/coordinator/plan`, `POST …/coordinator/approve`, and `PUT …/coordinator/pause` read and control the **Speaker emails** plan — the same plan that invites and reminds accepted speakers. Approving the plan via the API triggers a **202 needs_approval** gate, so an AI assistant's call is held for a human to confirm before emails go out.

where.path: Settings → API Tokens (org-wide keys with read:sessions / write:sessions scopes)

entries.use_case: Teams using AI assistants or custom integrations to manage their Sessions workspace can now import an event directly from its public URL and control the speaker email plan programmatically — without logging into the UI. The approval gate on the coordinator endpoint ensures no speaker emails go out until a human confirms.

cs_action.note: The import-url route and the approval gate depend on lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5420 shipping first. Until that PR is live, the import-url route returns 404 and the coordinator runs ungated. Confirm web-api is deployed before telling customers these routes are available.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is building an AI agent or integration that needs to set up Sessions events or manage speaker email plans without manual UI steps.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Sessions workspace API with org-wide keys who want to automate event import or speaker email plan management from an AI assistant or external system.
internal.gotchas: Requires lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5420 to be merged and deployed first. Until then, import-url returns 404 and the coordinator approval gate is not enforced. Org-wide keys only — event-scoped keys will not work.
internal.talk_track: Your AI assistant can now import a Sessions event straight from its public page URL and manage the speaker email plan — including pausing it or holding approval — all through the API, with a human-in-the-loop gate before any emails go out to speakers.

draft.docs_gap: The API changelog and reference should document the four new Sessions workspace routes (import-url with dryRun, coordinator GET/plan/approve/pause), their request/response shapes, the 202 needs_approval approval gate behaviour, and the org-wide key requirement.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessions workspace API lets you automate the full speaker management lifecycle from any AI assistant or integration. Import events, read and update the speaker email plan, and control when invitation and reminder emails go out — all with org-wide API keys and the same read:sessions / write:sessions scopes used across the workspace.

entries.title: Let AI assistants browse your program, hand off registration, and let attendees RSVP to sessions
entries.summary: When enabled for an event, AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT can read the public program (sessions, speakers, sponsors) and hand attendees off to the partner registration page with a tracked link. Attendees who verify their identity with a 6-digit email code can **RSVP** to or cancel individual sessions, view **My sessions**, and download a signed **.ics** calendar file. For events connected to Cvent or Swoogo, RSVPs are pushed live to the partner platform; Bizzabo and Swapcard support is in dry-run or deep-link mode. A **"Plan this event with Claude / ChatGPT"** panel is injected into the event's public pages via a snippet.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Agent-ready events; then Event Settings → Agent Settings

entries.use_case: Organizers who want attendees to plan their conference schedule through Claude or ChatGPT can turn on agent-ready events so AI assistants can browse sessions, hand off to registration, and let attendees RSVP to individual sessions — all without leaving their AI client.

cs_action.note: The feature is off by default and requires a super-user to turn on Event_Agent_Settings per event. Live partner RSVP push (Cvent, Swoogo) additionally requires partner_push_mode=live and working Apps-engine connections with vendor session IDs in Entity_Links. Bizzabo push is unverified; Swapcard uses a deep link only.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees can use Claude or ChatGPT to browse and plan their conference schedule, or when they want AI-assisted registration hand-off.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running large conferences on Cvent or Swoogo who want to offer AI-assisted session planning to attendees; also relevant for any event with a public program that wants a 'Plan with AI' entry point.
internal.staff_path: Event Settings → Agent Settings (super-user console only at launch)
internal.gotchas: Live RSVP push to Cvent and Swoogo requires the event's Apps-engine connection and vendor session IDs (Entity_Links) to be in place. Bizzabo push is a dry run — the endpoint is unverified. Swapcard only deep-links to its own agenda page. Attendees are never written to the CRM. The accessibility (axe) audit on the injected snippet is still outstanding.
internal.talk_track: Attendees can open Claude or ChatGPT, browse your full session catalog, and RSVP to the sessions they want to attend — all without touching your registration platform directly. For Cvent and Swoogo events, those RSVPs sync back to the partner platform in real time.

draft.docs_gap: The /attend/ai-assistants guide should add a section covering agent-ready events: how to turn it on, what the AI assistant can read (sessions, speakers, sponsors, off-record and draft exclusions), the registration hand-off flow and UTM/sb_ref tracking, attendee identity verification (6-digit email code), RSVP and cancel, My sessions, the signed .ics link, and per-partner push behaviour (Cvent live, Swoogo live, Bizzabo dry-run, Swapcard deep-link).
draft.why_use_it: Agent-ready events expose your public program — sessions, speakers, sponsors — to AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT so attendees can ask questions, build a personal schedule, and get a direct link to register, without leaving the assistant they already use. Attendees who verify their identity receive a session-scoped token that lets them RSVP to or cancel sessions and download a calendar file. For events on Cvent or Swoogo, those RSVPs flow directly into the partner platform in real time.

entries.title: CRM import preview correctly shows company rows and preserves people tags
entries.summary: Two fixes land in the CRM import preview. When previewing a company import using pre-supplied rows (rather than a CSV file), the preview now renders each row correctly with a line number instead of returning an empty result. When previewing a people import, **Tags** (roles) that were already attached to reviewed rows are now shown accurately in the preview — they were previously displayed as empty even though the import itself applied them correctly.
entries.use_case: Teams using the AI agent to run CRM import journeys can now trust that the import preview accurately reflects what will be imported — company rows supplied as structured data appear in the preview, and tags on people rows are shown correctly before confirming the import.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that their CRM import preview looked wrong — either blank company rows or missing tags on people — this fix resolves both.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the CRM add-on who runs imports via the AI agent or the import preview flow.
internal.staff_path: CRM → People → Import
internal.gotchas: The bug only affected the preview step; the actual import applied tags correctly all along. Customers who noticed the discrepancy and re-checked after importing would have found their data intact.

draft.docs_gap: The import guide should add a section describing the preview step — what each row shows, how line numbers appear, and how tags are reflected before confirming.

entries.title: Create a nomination on someone's behalf via the Awards Workspace API
entries.summary: A new `POST /v1/organization/:orgId/awards/workspace/programs/:programId/nominations` endpoint lets API clients submit a nomination on behalf of a nominee. The request body accepts the nominee's email and optional name, organisation and title, an optional nominator, category, form answers, and a `submit` flag to submit immediately. The response returns the submission ID, status, friendly ID and any missing fields. Requires a token with the `write:awards` scope.
entries.use_case: Teams that manage nominations through an external CRM, registration system or custom portal can now push nominations directly into an Awards program via the API — including pre-filling answers and auto-submitting — without requiring the nominee to visit the Sessionboard form.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to bulk-nominate members from their AMS or CRM, or wants to automate nominations from a registration workflow.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the Awards add-on who have a developer or integration partner and want to drive nominations from an external system.
internal.gotchas: The token must carry the write:awards scope; tokens without it will be rejected. The submit flag must be true to move the nomination out of draft; omitting it leaves it as an incomplete submission.
internal.talk_track: If you already have your nominees in a CRM or member database, you can now push them straight into your Awards program via the API — answers pre-filled, submitted and ready for your reviewers — without anyone having to fill in the form manually.

draft.docs_gap: The API changelog and the Awards managing-submissions guide should document the new POST nominations endpoint, its request body fields (nominee, nominator, categoryId, answers, submit), the required write:awards scope, and the shape of the response (submission id, status, friendly_id, missing_fields).
draft.why_use_it: The Awards Workspace API lets your systems create and manage nominations programmatically. Use it to integrate your CRM, member database or event registration platform so that eligible nominees are entered automatically, their form answers are pre-populated from data you already hold, and submissions land in Sessionboard ready for review without any manual re-entry.
